description: Towards a peer recorded Ed3 a segment is never shortened, so a first ARQ D_PDU too long for the configured transmission length still stretches the transmission to the whole blocks it needs.
note: As dts-tx-no-align-ed3-peer-arq up to its data transmission, with dts.max_segment_size 100 (C-0503) and dts.max_transmission_ms 5550 (one block: 600 + 4800 + 150), so one 64-byte block carries 64 bytes. Everything before 76500 is unchanged: our accept needs one block. At 76500 the whole 50-byte C_PDU is one segment, an 18 + 50 = 68-byte ED3-DATA-ONLY (type 0, C-0190, C-0730), FSN 0, C_PDU START and END, TX WIN LWE and UWE, DELIVER IN ORDER. It does not fit the one block the limit allows. Towards a peer recorded Ed3 the segment may not be shortened (C-0554, C-0870; interp C-1155), and the limit may not block it (C-0551, C-0878), so the transmission is made the whole blocks it needs, 2 (interp C-1042), 600 + 9600 + 150 = 10350 ms; EOT ceil(9750 / 500) = 20 (C-0104, C-1043). The 60 spare bytes take no PADDING towards an Ed3 peer (C-0367, C-0055, C-1154) and there is no acknowledgement to repeat, so they are zero filled. dts.ack_wait/0.0.1.3 starts when the transmission ends at 86850; nothing else is queued. Towards a peer recorded Ed4 the segment would instead be cut to the one block (as in dts-tx-ed4-first-segment-cut-to-limit).
